newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan minister seeks 7-8 pct GPD growth.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan minister seeks 7-8 pct GPD growth.

text.p: Moroccan Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj said on Thursday the country's economy needed to grow by seven to eight percent a year to be competitive in an international free market.
Kabbaj, who was addressing a three-day meeting on the Moroccan economy, said the country was at a crossroads and needed to cut its budget deficit to ensure decent development.
"Morocco's economy should reach at least seven to eight percent in future in GDP from the average three to four percent in recent years," Kabbaj told the meeting.
Morocco expects a budget deficit of around 3.0 percent of GDP in 1996 compared with a deficit of 5.3 percent of GDP last year.
"If we maintain a positive growth in the coming decade, the GDP could reach at least $3,000 per head from the present $1,200," the minister said.
Faster growth would improve living standards of Morocco's 27 million population and create a healthy climate for competition, he said.

Growth in GDP is expected to top 10 percent this year after a figure of minus 7.6 percent because of drought. Uneven weather conditions have caused massive fluctuations in economic growth, with GDP falling 1.1 percent in 1993 and then shoooting up by 11.5 percent in 1994.
In recent years, the government succeeded in keeping the budget deficit under tight control despite the negative impact of the weather on the economy, Kabbaj said. Kabbaj's speech
was in line with the government campaign to encourage public and private sectors to change their behaviour and draw a long-term strategy for sustainable growth and competitiveness.

"Without sustained economic growth and a rise in direct foreign investments, the economy cannot provide jobs and the percentage of unemployment would reach 25 percent in the next decade from 16 percent in 1996," Kabbaj said.
